title: UserDefaults with a Typed Wrapper
hints: A property wrapper can read and write `UserDefaults` in its `wrappedValue`.
Encode values as JSON `Data` so any `Codable` type works; return the default when missing.
A fresh `Preferences()` reads what the previous one saved.
jsBridge: A `@propertyWrapper` around `UserDefaults` gives typed, defaulted settings, like wrapping `localStorage` with JSON (de)serialisation and defaults. Swift makes it declarative per property.

compass.q: JS `localStorage` stores strings only; you JSON-wrap everything. How does `Codable` make the Swift wrapper generic?
What happens if a stored value no longer decodes after a model change? What should the wrapper return?
Custom wrapper vs `@AppStorage`: when do you need the custom one (non-SwiftUI code, Codable types)?
What must never go in `UserDefaults`? (Secrets. It's a plain plist on disk.)
